capabilities.name: fr.button
capabilities.summary: Momentary push button with debounced edges and gesture recognition.
capabilities.doc:
`down` fires on the debounced leading edge and is the lowest-latency signal — bind game
input to it. `click` is semantic; with multi_press_max > 1 it waits multi_press_gap_ms
to tell single from double clicks.

config.name: long_press_ms
config.doc: 0 disables long_press

config.name: multi_press_max
config.doc: 1 = click on release, no wait

commands.name: inject
commands.doc:
Replays a gesture through ButtonService exactly as a real one, including `pressed`.
press/release emit only down/up and set/clear `pressed` (hold a button for a test).

capabilities.name: fr.led
capabilities.summary: A single indicator light (mono or RGB, optionally dimmable) with on-device effects.

config.name: max_brightness
config.doc: hard cap (WS2812 boards default to 64)

commands.name: blink
commands.doc: Flash `count` times (0 = until stop/set), then restore the steady state and emit effect_done.

capabilities.name: fr.display
capabilities.summary: A pixel panel with drawing primitives everywhere and LVGL layouts where the panel's driver says so (trait ui).
capabilities.doc:
Colours are 0xRRGGBB on the wire; a mono panel (color mono1) lights a pixel whose colour is at least 50 % luminance.
Commands are queued to the renderer and never draw inside dispatch; the panel is flushed at most every flush_ms.
Primitives (clear, text, fill_rect) work on every panel. ui_load and ui_set answer UNSUPPORTED where `ui` is false
(the C3 OLED's built-in 1-bit renderer); on LVGL panels a layout replaces the screen and primitives sent after it
draw on top. snapshot and snapshot_read read back the framebuffer as drawn (test builds), so an agent sees the real
screen and compares it with the desktop render of the same commands (T-DISPLAY).

UiWidget.doc: One widget: `id` names it for ui_set and ui events; button, slider and switch emit ui events when touched.

fields.name: w
fields.doc: 0: sized to its content

fields.name: h
fields.doc: 0: sized to its content

fields.name: text
fields.doc: label and button text

fields.name: value
fields.doc: bar, slider, arc: the value; switch: 0 off, else on

fields.name: min
fields.doc: bar, slider, arc: the range's bottom

fields.name: max
fields.doc: bar, slider, arc: the range's top

fields.name: color
fields.doc: text, indicator or fill colour

fields.name: bg
fields.doc: background colour

fields.name: font
fields.doc: 0: 14 px, 1: 20 px, 2: 28 px (the built-in Montserrat sizes)

fields.name: align
fields.doc: text alignment inside the widget

UiLayout.doc: A screen: its background and up to 24 widgets, drawn in order (later ones on top).

fields.name: bg
fields.doc: screen background

config.name: rotation
config.doc: panel rotation; a board entry's `rotation` (0, 90, 180, 270) is its default

config.name: brightness
config.doc: backlight level at boot; ignored on panels without backlight control

config.name: max_brightness
config.doc: a hard cap on the backlight: set_brightness and brightness scale into 0..max (design lcd-clock-c1 D4; 128 where the vendor warns against full brightness)

config.name: flush_ms
config.doc: coalescing period: the panel is flushed at most this often (50 Hz)

properties.name: brightness
properties.doc: the backlight level (255 on panels without backlight control)

commands.name: clear
commands.doc: Drops every primitive and any layout, and fills the panel with `color`.

commands.name: text
commands.doc: A text primitive at (x, y), its top left. Size 1 is the panel's smallest font (LVGL: Montserrat 14/20/28 for sizes 1-3, 28 for 4; the C3: 5x7 glyphs scaled by size).

commands.name: fill_rect
commands.doc: A filled rectangle primitive.

commands.name: set_brightness
commands.doc: Sets the backlight (property brightness); accepted and ignored on panels without backlight control.

commands.name: ui_load
commands.doc: Replaces the screen with `layout` (LVGL panels; UNSUPPORTED where trait ui is false). BULK: TCP or serial, never over a gateway; the layout must fit one BULK frame.

commands.name: ui_set
commands.doc: Updates widget `id`: `fields` says which of the others are set (1 text, 2 value, 4 color, 8 visible). NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; UNSUPPORTED where trait ui is false.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: bit mask: 1 text, 2 value, 4 color, 8 visible

commands.name: snapshot
commands.doc: The framebuffer as drawn: its CRC-32 (IEEE, as zlib) and size. Read it with snapshot_read; T-DISPLAY compares the CRC with the desktop render's. BULK like snapshot_read: a device reachable only through a gateway is refused before a frame is frozen that no read could fetch.

result.name: format
result.doc: mono1: 1 bit per pixel, rows packed MSB first; rgb565: 2 bytes per pixel, little-endian

commands.name: snapshot_read
commands.doc: A chunk of the framebuffer of the last snapshot (BULK: TCP or serial).

events.name: ui
events.doc: A widget was touched (or an injected touch hit it); `value` is the slider's or switch's new value.

capabilities.name: fr.audio_out
capabilities.summary: A speaker or line output that plays a tone made on the node, or PCM it pulls from the hub over HTTP.
capabilities.doc:
Design audio-a1 D2-D5. `tone` needs no network. `play` makes the node GET raw PCM (s16le mono at `sample_hz`) from the
hub's HTTP listener (`GET /v1/audio/out/<play_id>`), which converted the source to that rate; PCM never travels on
the hub link. One sound at a time: a new tone or play replaces the one playing (play_done reason stopped).
play_done reports how each ended; a tone's play_id is 0.

config.name: volume
config.doc: volume at boot

config.name: sample_hz
config.doc: one of 8000, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100, 48000; the rate tones are made at

commands.name: tone
commands.doc: A sine of freq_hz for ms, made on the node at config sample_hz; answers when it starts. volume overrides the current volume for this tone only.

commands.name: play
commands.doc: Plays PCM the hub serves at GET /v1/audio/out/<play_id> (design D3). Dispatch never blocks: OK once the fr_stream task has the play, INVALID_ARGS for a rate the driver does not take. A GET that fails ends it with play_done net_lost (samples 0).

fields.name: play_id
fields.doc: issued by the hub; the GET path names it

fields.name: sample_hz
fields.doc: the PCM's rate, one of the config's rates

commands.name: stop
commands.doc: Stops the tone or play (play_done reason stopped); OK when nothing plays.

commands.name: set_volume
commands.doc: Sets the volume (property volume) for what plays now and later.

events.name: play_done
events.doc: A tone or play ended: done, stopped (stop, or replaced), net_lost, underrun (the stream starved for good), error. underruns counts the silent gaps played.

fields.name: play_id
fields.doc: 0 for a tone

fields.name: samples
fields.doc: samples played

capabilities.name: fr.analog_in
capabilities.summary: An analog input sampled on the node and reported as a normalised, rate-limited value.
capabilities.doc:
`value` is a LATEST property (latest wins, never retried), so a fast stream never queues behind itself.
It is the input's calibrated voltage mapped from [min_mv, max_mv] onto 0..65535 and clamped.
Use `crossed` events for thresholds that must not be missed: they are reliable and carry hysteresis.

config.name: report_hz
config.doc: max STATE rate. Provisional until S2 (C4)

config.name: deadband
config.doc: in value units; a change smaller than this since the last report is not reported. Provisional until S2

config.name: filter
config.doc: ema: alpha 1/4

config.name: min_mv
config.doc: maps to value 0

config.name: max_mv
config.doc: maps to value 65535; must exceed min_mv

config.name: hysteresis
config.doc: in value units, for `crossed`

config.name: thresholds
config.doc: value thresholds that emit `crossed`

properties.name: value
properties.doc: 0..65535 over [min_mv, max_mv], after calibration and filter

commands.name: inject
commands.doc: Holds `value` in place of the ADC for hold_ms (0 means 1,000 ms; at most 60,000). A newer inject replaces it.

commands.name: read
commands.doc: The current reading, unfiltered and filtered. Answered from the last sample; never touches the ADC.

capabilities.name: fr.audio_in
capabilities.summary: A microphone (or any analog signal at audio rate) sampled on the node, its level reported, its PCM streamed to the hub over a separate HTTP connection or routed to an output on the same node.
capabilities.doc:
Design audio-a1 D1, D3-D5. PCM never travels on the hub link: stream_start makes the node POST it to the hub's HTTP
listener (`POST /v1/audio/in/<stream_id>`, chunked, s16le mono at the stream's rate), and stream_ended reports how
it ended. A stream id is one the hub issued; one stream at a time (BUSY otherwise). Samples lost to a Wi-Fi stall
are counted in dropped_samples and the hub writes silence for them, so a recording keeps its length.
`level` is a LATEST property (RMS over the last 1/level_hz s, in dBFS x 10) while the microphone runs.
1.1 (design audio-a2 D3, additive): the on-board monitor. monitor_start routes this input's converted samples (after
the DC blocker and gain_db) into an fr.audio_out instance's play ring on the same node, inside the fr_audio task: no
network, no hub. The output must run this input's sample_hz (both configs; INVALID_ARGS otherwise). While a monitor
runs the output is busy: a play or tone on it ends the monitor (monitor_ended busy), and monitor_start refuses an
output that plays (BUSY). `level` reports pause while monitoring (the board's own traffic stays at its heartbeat).

config.name: sample_hz
config.doc: one of 8000, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100, 48000; a stream may ask for another

config.name: gain_db
config.doc: digital gain applied in the 32 -> 16-bit conversion

config.name: hpf_hz
config.doc: DC blocker corner; 0: off

config.name: level_hz
config.doc: `level` reports per second while the microphone runs; 0: none

properties.name: level
properties.doc: RMS over the last 1/level_hz s, dBFS x 10 (-900 is silence); paused while monitoring

properties.name: monitoring
properties.doc: a monitor runs (1.1): monitor_start to monitor_ended

commands.name: stream_start
commands.doc: Starts streaming to the hub over HTTP (design D3). Dispatch never blocks: OK once the fr_stream task has the stream, BUSY while another runs (or a monitor runs at another rate), INVALID_ARGS for a rate the driver does not take. A connection that cannot be opened ends the stream with stream_ended net_lost (samples 0).

fields.name: stream_id
fields.doc: issued by the hub; the POST path names it

fields.name: seconds
fields.doc: 0: until stream_stop

fields.name: sample_hz
fields.doc: absent: config sample_hz; one of the config's rates

commands.name: stream_stop
commands.doc: Ends stream `stream_id` (stream_ended reason stopped); NOT_FOUND when it is not the running stream.

commands.name: level_get
commands.doc: The level now, in dBFS x 10, and the clipped samples since the microphone started; starts the microphone for 200 ms when it is idle.

commands.name: monitor_start
commands.doc: Routes this input to fr.audio_out port to_port on the same node (1.1, design audio-a2 D3). Dispatch never blocks: OK once fr_audio has the monitor. INVALID_ARGS: to_port is not an fr.audio_out instance, or its sample_hz differs from this input's. BUSY: this input already monitors, or streams at another rate; or the output plays, or another input monitors to it. Ends with monitor_ended.

fields.name: to_port
fields.doc: the fr.audio_out instance's capability port

fields.name: seconds
fields.doc: 0: until monitor_stop

fields.name: volume
fields.doc: 0: the output's own volume; else this monitor's only

commands.name: monitor_stop
commands.doc: Ends the monitor (monitor_ended reason stopped); OK when none runs.

events.name: stream_ended
events.doc: A stream ended: stopped (stream_stop), done (`seconds` reached), net_lost (a send stalled 3 s or the connection dropped), overflow, error.

fields.name: samples
fields.doc: samples covered by the stream, dropped ones included

fields.name: dropped_samples
fields.doc: samples lost to ring overflows (the hub writes silence for them)

events.name: monitor_ended
events.doc: A monitor ended (1.1): stopped (monitor_stop), done (`seconds` reached), busy (a play or tone took the output), error (the source or the output failed).

fields.name: to_port
fields.doc: the output it fed

fields.name: samples
fields.doc: samples routed to the output

capabilities.name: fr.touch
capabilities.summary: A touch panel's single pointer, in its display's coordinates, with gestures.
capabilities.doc:
Coordinates are rotated to the display the instance is bound to (config `display`, that instance's port), so a
touch at (x, y) is the pixel (x, y) of that panel's fr.display. The LVGL renderer of that panel reads the same
touches as its pointer input, so a touched button emits fr.display `ui` events too.

config.name: display
config.doc: port of the fr.display instance this panel covers (0: none); codegen checks it names one

commands.name: inject
commands.doc: A touch at (x, y) as `gesture`, fed to the same path as the panel's (events, property, the LVGL pointer). A swipe starts at (x, y).

capabilities.name: fr.csi
capabilities.summary: Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI) captured on the node, its motion and RSSI reported, its raw records streamed to the hub over a separate HTTP connection.
capabilities.doc:
Design csi-c1 D7, D8, D10, D11, §12. The node keeps the CSI of the frames its source names: `router` pings the
default gateway rate_hz times a second and keeps the frames from the AP's BSSID; `peer` keeps the frames from
peer_mac (a board running fr.radio_tx); `any` keeps every frame's, its sender's MAC in the record. Capture runs from
the moment the station has an IP until reboot, so the properties are live without a stream; `motion` is the mean
absolute change of the subcarrier amplitudes against an exponential baseline (about 2 s), normalised to 0..65535,
reported at features_hz. Records never travel on the hub link: stream_start makes the node POST them to the hub's
HTTP listener (`POST /v1/stream/in/<stream_id>`, chunked, X-Fr-Kind csi, X-Fr-Format csi1; the block and record
layout in design csi-c1 §12), and stream_ended reports how it ended. A stream id is one the hub issued; one stream
at a time (BUSY otherwise). Records lost to a Wi-Fi stall are counted in `dropped`, never filled in.
A stream may name its own source and peer for its length (a live view switching router and peer); capture and the
features follow it, and return to the config's at its end.

config.name: source
config.doc: router: pings to the default gateway; peer: frames from peer_mac; any: every frame

config.name: rate_hz
config.doc: router: pings per second (a router may answer fewer; `rate` shows what came)

config.name: peer_mac
config.doc: peer: the transmitter's station MAC, 6 bytes; empty: none (source peer then needs a stream's peer_mac)

config.name: format
config.doc: the CSI asked of the hardware; auto keeps every format the frames carry

config.name: features_hz
config.doc: `motion`, `rssi` and `rate` reports per second

properties.name: motion
properties.doc: 0..65535: the mean absolute amplitude change against the ~2 s baseline, normalised; a still room reads low

properties.name: rssi
properties.doc: mean RSSI of the kept frames over the last report window

properties.name: rate
properties.doc: CSI records kept per second over the last report window

commands.name: stream_start
commands.doc: Starts streaming records to the hub over HTTP (design csi-c1 D11). Dispatch never blocks: OK once the fr_stream task has the stream, BUSY while another runs, INVALID_ARGS for source peer without a 6-byte peer_mac (here or in config). A connection that cannot be opened ends the stream with stream_ended net_lost (records 0).

fields.name: stream_id
fields.doc: issued by the hub; the POST path names it

fields.name: seconds
fields.doc: 0: until stream_stop

fields.name: source
fields.doc: absent: config source; for this stream only

fields.name: peer_mac
fields.doc: absent: config peer_mac; for this stream only

commands.name: stream_stop
commands.doc: Ends stream `stream_id` (stream_ended reason stopped); NOT_FOUND when it is not the running stream.

commands.name: baseline_reset
commands.doc: `motion`'s baseline becomes the amplitudes now (after someone left the room, or the board was moved).

events.name: stream_ended
events.doc: A stream ended: stopped (stream_stop), done (`seconds` reached), net_lost (a send stalled 3 s or the connection dropped), error (capture failed).

fields.name: records
fields.doc: records covered by the stream, dropped ones included

fields.name: dropped
fields.doc: records lost to ring overflows (a jump of a block's first_index)

capabilities.name: fr.radio_tx
capabilities.summary: A transmitter that sends ESP-NOW frames at a fixed rate toward one station, as the sensed source of a CSI receiver.
capabilities.doc:
Design csi-c1 D9. start sends ESP-NOW unicast frames of `len` bytes to peer_mac rate_hz times a second, at the robust
rate of the band (2.4 GHz: 11b 1 Mbps; 5 GHz: 11a 6 Mbps), on the channel the node's station is on, for `seconds`;
the receiver's fr.csi with source peer keeps their CSI. Frames carry no meaning (a sequence number, then zeros); a
frame the peer does not acknowledge is not sent again. Both boards must be on one channel: on 2.4 GHz any two nodes
of the fleet's network, on 5 GHz two 5 GHz-capable ones (a second C5). One run at a time: a start replaces the
running one. `sending` follows it.

properties.name: sending
properties.doc: a start runs: start to its seconds, a stop, or the station leaving its channel

commands.name: start
commands.doc: Starts sending (replacing a running start). INVALID_ARGS: peer_mac is not 6 bytes, or is a group address; BUSY: the station is not connected (no channel to send on).

fields.name: peer_mac
fields.doc: the receiver's station MAC

fields.name: len
fields.doc: payload bytes per frame (ESP-NOW v1's limit is 250)

fields.name: seconds
fields.doc: 0: until stop

commands.name: stop
commands.doc: Stops sending; OK when nothing is sent.

capabilities.name: fr.camera
capabilities.summary: A camera module that photographs on request, streams a live JPEG view to the hub, and records to its own micro-SD card for the hub to collect later.
capabilities.doc:
Design camera-c1 D7, D8, D10, §10. The sensor (an OV2640 on the AI-Thinker ESP32-CAM) is read through the chip's
DVP interface and delivers JPEG frames; the module keeps `frames`, `fps_x10` and `last_bytes` live. Frames never
travel on the hub link: stream_start makes the node POST them to the hub's HTTP listener (`POST /v1/stream/in/
<stream_id>`, chunked, X-Fr-Kind jpeg, X-Fr-Format mjpg1: one frame per chunk behind a 24-byte head, design
camera-c1 D10) and/or write them to the card (`/sdcard/fr/<stream_id 8 hex>/<index 6 digits>.jpg`), as `to` says.
A snapshot is a stream of max_frames 1; a timelapse a stream with interval_ms; a recording a stream `to sd` that
runs without the hub. One stream at a time (BUSY otherwise); a stream id is one the hub issued. The card is
mounted at boot when config `sd` is true (a missing card is CardState none, not an error); recordings on it are
listed with sd_list, fetched to the hub with sd_fetch (an mjpg1 stream whose frames carry flags b0) and removed
with sd_delete. `set` changes the sensor now and keeps the settings until reboot; frame sizes above the trait
max_frame_size (the size the frame buffers were made for at init) are INVALID_ARGS.

Recording.doc: A recording on the card: the stream_id that made it (its directory name, 8 hex), its frame count and their total bytes.

traits.name: sensor
traits.doc: the sensor fitted: 1 ov2640 (from the board entry; 0 unknown)

traits.name: max_frame_size
traits.doc: the largest frame_size the buffers take (config max_frame_size)

config.name: frame_size
config.doc: the frame size at boot (800x600); `set` changes it until reboot

config.name: max_frame_size
config.doc: the frame buffers are sized for this at init; frame_size never exceeds it

config.name: quality
config.doc: JPEG quality, lower is better (esp32-camera's scale)

config.name: fb_count
config.doc: frame buffers (PSRAM); 2 lets the sensor fill one while the other is sent

config.name: vflip
config.doc: flip the image vertically

config.name: hmirror
config.doc: mirror the image horizontally

config.name: xclk_hz
config.doc: the sensor's clock from the chip (XCLK, an LEDC channel); 20 MHz on the OV2640

config.name: sd
config.doc: mount the card at boot; a missing card is CardState none, not an error. false: the card is never touched (sd_* answer UNSUPPORTED)

properties.name: frames
properties.doc: frames captured since boot

properties.name: fps_x10
properties.doc: frames per second over the last second, x10 (0 while idle)

properties.name: last_bytes
properties.doc: the last frame's JPEG bytes

properties.name: streaming
properties.doc: a stream (or an sd_fetch) runs

properties.name: sd
properties.doc: the card: none (no card, or config sd false), mounted, error (mount or write failed)

properties.name: sd_free_mb
properties.doc: free space on the card; 0 when none

commands.name: stream_start
commands.doc: Starts a stream of JPEG frames (design camera-c1 D8): to the hub over HTTP (an mjpg1 POST to /v1/stream/in/<stream_id>), to the card (a recording named by the stream id), or both. Dispatch never blocks: OK once the fr_stream task has it, BUSY while another runs, INVALID_ARGS for `to` sd or both with no card mounted, or a frame_size above the trait max_frame_size. interval_ms paces by each frame's start time (0: as fast as the sensor and the path allow); seconds and max_frames end it done (0: no limit, until stream_stop).

fields.name: stream_id
fields.doc: issued by the hub; the POST path and the recording's directory name it

fields.name: seconds
fields.doc: 0: until stream_stop (or max_frames)

fields.name: interval_ms
fields.doc: time between frame starts; 0: as fast as the path allows (a live view)

fields.name: max_frames
fields.doc: frames to take; 0: no limit. 1 is a snapshot

fields.name: frame_size
fields.doc: absent: the current frame_size (config, or the last set); for this stream only

fields.name: quality
fields.doc: absent: the current quality; for this stream only

commands.name: stream_stop
commands.doc: Ends stream `stream_id` (stream_ended reason stopped); NOT_FOUND when it is not the running stream.

commands.name: set
commands.doc: Changes the sensor's settings now and keeps them until reboot (absent fields stay). INVALID_ARGS for a frame_size above the trait max_frame_size. A running stream takes the new settings from its next frame.

commands.name: sd_list
commands.doc: The recordings on the card, oldest first, from the `from`-th (0: the first): at most 64 per answer, `next` the index to ask for the rest (0: none left). UNSUPPORTED without a card (property sd none or error). BULK: TCP or serial, never over a gateway.

result.name: next
result.doc: the `from` of the next page; 0: this was the last

commands.name: sd_fetch
commands.doc: Streams recording `recording`'s frames to the hub as an mjpg1 stream (flags b0 set), from frame `from_frame`; ends done after the last. BUSY while a stream runs; NOT_FOUND for a recording not on the card; UNSUPPORTED without a card.

fields.name: stream_id
fields.doc: issued by the hub; the POST path names it

fields.name: recording
fields.doc: the recording's id (its stream_id when made)

commands.name: sd_delete
commands.doc: Removes recording `recording` from the card (its directory and frames); OK when it is already gone. UNSUPPORTED without a card; BUSY while a stream writes to or reads from it.

events.name: stream_ended
events.doc: A stream (or sd_fetch) ended: stopped (stream_stop), done (`seconds` or `max_frames` reached), net_lost (a send stalled 3 s or the connection dropped), overflow (the card is full or failed mid-stream), error (the sensor failed).

fields.name: frames
fields.doc: frames the stream covered, dropped ones included (the index it reached)

fields.name: dropped
fields.doc: frames the sensor delivered that the stream could not take (the hub path behind)

fields.name: bytes
fields.doc: JPEG bytes sent and/or written

capabilities.name: fr.scale
capabilities.summary: A weighing scale - a load cell through a 24-bit bridge ADC (HX711), tared and calibrated on the node, reported in milligrams.
capabilities.doc:
`weight_mg` is a LATEST property (latest wins, never retried) reported at most `report_hz` times a second when it
moved at least `deadband_mg`, so a fast stream never queues behind itself. `settled` is the reliable signal that
something was put on or taken off. The part converts at its own rate (the HX711's RATE pin: 10 or 80 per second);
`rate_hz` says what it does. `tare` and `calibrate` average the last `samples` conversions the node already holds,
so they answer at once; they answer BUSY while the reading is not stable. The offset and the scale factor they set
are kept across reboots (NVS) until `reset_calibration`. `watch_start` raises the report rate for a bounded time
(a recording of every conversion) and falls back by itself.

config.name: report_hz
config.doc: max STATE rate outside a watch; at or above the part's rate (96 at its 80 Hz setting) every conversion is reported

config.name: deadband_mg
config.doc: a change smaller than this since the last report is not reported (outside a watch)

config.name: filter
config.doc: ema: alpha 1/4; median5: the median of the last 5 conversions

config.name: gain
config.doc: the channel and gain the clock train selects: a128 (channel A, 128), a64, b32 (channel B, 32)

config.name: counts_per_kg
config.doc: the scale factor until a calibration is made: raw counts per kilogram (a typical 1-5 kg bar cell at gain 128, inferred)

config.name: stable_mg
config.doc: stable: the filtered weight stayed within this of its mean for stable_ms

config.name: settle_min_mg
config.doc: `settled` fires only for a stable weight at least this far from the last settled one

properties.name: weight_mg
properties.doc: tared, calibrated and filtered

properties.name: calibrated
properties.doc: a calibration was made and is kept (else config counts_per_kg)

properties.name: rate_hz
properties.doc: conversions over the last second: 80 or 10 by the part's RATE pin, 0 when the part does not answer

commands.name: tare
commands.doc: The mean raw reading of the last `samples` conversions becomes zero, and is kept across reboots. BUSY while the reading is not stable or fewer conversions are held; FAILED when the part does not answer.

commands.name: calibrate
commands.doc: With a known mass on the tared scale: the scale factor from the mean of the last `samples` conversions, kept across reboots. BUSY while not stable; INVALID_ARGS for known_mg 0 or a reading at the offset (nothing on the scale).

commands.name: read
commands.doc: The last conversion and the calibration in use. Answered from what the node holds; never touches the part.

result.name: raw
result.doc: the last conversion, sign-extended from 24 bits

commands.name: reset_calibration
commands.doc: Offset 0 and config counts_per_kg again; the kept calibration is erased.

commands.name: watch_start
commands.doc: Reports every change up to report_hz (no deadband) for `seconds`, then falls back to config by itself. A newer watch_start replaces the running one.

commands.name: watch_stop
commands.doc: Ends a watch now; OK when none runs.

commands.name: inject
commands.doc: Holds `weight_mg` in place of the part for hold_ms (0 means 1,000 ms; at most 60,000). A newer inject replaces it.

events.name: settled
events.doc: The weight became stable at least settle_min_mg away from the last settled weight: something was put on or taken off.

fields.name: delta_mg
fields.doc: from the last settled weight (the first after boot: from 0)

capabilities.name: fr.battery
capabilities.summary: A rechargeable cell (Li-ion, LiFePO4 or a lithium-ion capacitor) - its voltage, its charger's state, levels and a floor the node enforces.
capabilities.doc:
Design power-p1 D2-D5. `mv` is a LATEST property reported at most `report_hz` times a second when it moved at least
`deadband_mv`; `charger` and `level` change with reliable events (`charge`, `level_change`) so they are never missed. The
node samples 10 times a second whatever report_hz is, and protects the cell on its own: at `floor_mv` the test load
goes off, every fr.haptic drawing from this instance stops and `protect` fires; fr.haptic refuses to start at or
below `critical_mv`. The voltages default by chemistry (0 = the chemistry's value): liion 4200/3500/3300/3000,
lifepo4 3600/3000/2800/2500, lic 4000/3000/2800/2700 (full/low/critical/floor); full_mv above the chemistry's
maximum (4250/3650/4200) is refused. `calibrate` takes a multimeter reading and keeps the divider in NVS until
`reset_calibration`. Ten failed readings in a row make the reading stale: the test load goes off and loads are
refused until one succeeds. While an inject holds, levels follow the lower of the held and the real voltage.

traits.name: status_pins
traits.doc: CHRG and STDBY are wired (else charger is always none)

traits.name: test_load
traits.doc: a switched test load is wired (the load command)

traits.name: charge_gate
traits.doc: a charge gate is wired (the gate command, charge_to_mv)

config.name: full_mv
config.doc: 100 %; 0 = the chemistry's

config.name: low_mv
config.doc: level low below this; 0 = the chemistry's

config.name: critical_mv
config.doc: level critical below this, loads refused; 0 = the chemistry's

config.name: floor_mv
config.doc: level empty below this, loads cut; 0 = the chemistry's

config.name: divider_milli
config.doc: the sense divider x1000 until a calibration is made

config.name: charge_to_mv
config.doc: with a gate: charging stops here; 0 = full_mv

config.name: load_ohm
config.doc: the test load's resistance, for the hub's capacity arithmetic; 0 = unknown

properties.name: mv
properties.doc: calibrated, 8 conversions, EMA 1/4

properties.name: percent
properties.doc: from the chemistry's table (the hub refines it from a cell's learned curve)

properties.name: level
properties.doc: 50 mV hysteresis upward

properties.name: load_on
properties.doc: the test load is on

properties.name: gate_open
properties.doc: the charge gate is open

commands.name: read
commands.doc: The last sample and the calibration in use. Never touches the ADC.

result.name: adc_mv
result.doc: at the pin, before the divider

commands.name: calibrate
commands.doc: The divider becomes meter_mv / adc_mv (a multimeter on the cell), kept across reboots. BUSY with no sample yet; INVALID_ARGS when the result is more than 15 % from config divider_milli (a typo in the reading).

commands.name: reset_calibration
commands.doc: Config divider_milli again; the kept calibration is erased.

commands.name: load
commands.doc: The test load on for at most `seconds` (0 means 60), or off; while it is on, `on` renews its time at any level above empty. It also goes off at the floor, on a stale reading, at boot, and 60 s after the newest frame of the hub that turned it on (or at a new hub run). UNSUPPORTED without a load; BUSY turning it on at or below critical.

commands.name: gate
commands.doc: Opens or closes the charge gate by hand. An open gate still closes at charge_to_mv; a hand close stands until the charger's state changes. UNSUPPORTED without a gate; BUSY opening it at or above charge_to_mv.

commands.name: inject
commands.doc: Holds mv (and the charger state when charger_set) in place of the hardware for hold_ms (0 means 1,000; at most 60,000). Protection acts on injected values as on real ones.

fields.name: charger_set
fields.doc: false: the charger keeps reading the pins

events.name: charge
events.doc: The charger's state changed (held 300 ms before it counts).

events.name: level_change
events.doc: The level changed (low, critical, empty, or back to ok).

events.name: protect
events.doc: The node cut loads at the floor (floor) or closed the gate above full (ceiling) on its own.

capabilities.name: fr.haptic
capabilities.summary: A vibration motor (ERM) or a solenoid on one switched output, compensated for and protected by the cell it draws from.
capabilities.doc:
Design power-p1 D6-D7. The duty is level% x rated_mv / supply_mv (capped at 100 %), recomputed every 10 ms from the
supply's (an fr.battery instance named by `supply`) latest sample, so an ERM feels the same across the cell's range
and never sees more than its rating on average. A solenoid pulls in at 100 % for kick_ms, then holds at hold_pct.
`pulse` and `play` answer BUSY at or below the supply's critical voltage (a solenoid below critical + 300 mV), with
no fresh supply reading, or past the cooldown budget (cooldown_pct of any 10 s); a running one is stopped by the
supply falling to critical or its floor, or by max_on_ms of on-time without a break, with `cut`. A program started
while a hub session existed stops (no `cut`) 10 s after that hub's newest frame or at a new hub run.

traits.name: pwm
traits.doc: the output is PWM (level and compensation); else on/off only

config.name: rated_mv
config.doc: the load's rated voltage: 100 % level averages this

config.name: supply
config.doc: the fr.battery instance it draws from; empty = none (no compensation, no protection)

config.name: max_on_ms
config.doc: longest on-time without a break (steps that run into each other count as one); 0 = 10,000 for erm, 1,000 for solenoid

config.name: kick_ms
config.doc: solenoid: full power for this long; at most max_on_ms

config.name: hold_pct
config.doc: solenoid: the level after the kick

config.name: cooldown_pct
config.doc: most of any 10 s the load may be on; 0 = 100 for erm, 30 for solenoid

properties.name: supply_mv
properties.doc: the supply's voltage, reported while active and at its end

commands.name: pulse
commands.doc: On for `ms` at `level` % (1-100, default 100), replacing whatever runs. BUSY at or below the supply's critical, or past the cooldown budget; INVALID_ARGS above max_on_ms.

commands.name: play
commands.doc: A pattern: steps are on, off, on, off... in ms (at most 32), played `repeat` times (default 1), replacing whatever runs. BUSY as pulse; INVALID_ARGS for no steps or an on-step above max_on_ms, and for a solenoid a zero off-step or an odd number of steps with repeat > 1.

commands.name: stop
commands.doc: Off now; OK when nothing runs.

events.name: cut
events.doc: A running pulse or pattern was stopped by the supply or by max_on_ms.

capabilities.name: fr.storage
capabilities.summary: Files on a removable FAT card (micro-SD) - listed, read, written and removed from the hub in chunks.
capabilities.doc:
Design lcd-clock-c1 D5-D6 (as built). Paths are absolute under the card ("/" is its root): ASCII, at most 96 bytes, no
"..", no backslash; anything else is INVALID_ARGS. Each command does one bounded piece of I/O (a chunk, a directory
page); the mount and the free-space walk run in the background, and while one runs (`busy`) every command answers BUSY.
Without card detect a removal is noticed by the next access that fails while the card no longer answers (unmounted
{reason: removed}); other failures (a full card, a read-only file, no memory) answer their error and keep the card.
`info` and `remount` mount again when the state is none. There is no format command.

Entry.doc: One directory entry: its name (not the path), size in bytes (0 for a directory), whether it is a directory, and its modification time (unix s, 0 when unknown).

traits.name: card_detect
traits.doc: a card-detect switch is wired (else removal is found on access)

config.name: max_files
config.doc: files open at once (FatFs keeps about 4 KB each)

config.name: chunk
config.doc: the most bytes one read or write carries

properties.name: free_mb
properties.doc: refreshed after writes, at most every 10 s

commands.name: info
commands.doc: The card's state and sizes (the cached ones; a refresh follows in the reports when they are old). With no card it starts a mount and answers BUSY while it runs; an attempt that ended under 3 s ago is not repeated.

result.name: name
result.doc: the card's product name from its CID

commands.name: list
commands.doc: A directory's entries from `offset`, at most 16; `more` when there are others.

commands.name: stat
commands.doc: One path's entry; NOT_FOUND when there is none.

commands.name: read
commands.doc: Up to `len` bytes (at most config chunk) from `offset`; `eof` when the file ends within them.

commands.name: write
commands.doc: Writes `data` at `offset` (creating the file and the directories on the way); `truncate` cuts the file at offset + its length. The data must not exceed config chunk; an offset past the file's end, or a card too full for the data, is INVALID_ARGS.

result.name: size
result.doc: the file's size after the write

commands.name: remove
commands.doc: A file, or an empty directory.

commands.name: remount
commands.doc: Unmounts (if mounted) and starts a mount in the background; answers the state now (none), `mounted` follows when it succeeds.

capabilities.name: fr.clock
capabilities.summary: A battery-backed real-time clock (DS3231) - its time, set from the hub to the second boundary, its temperature, oscillator-stop detection and aging trim.
capabilities.doc:
Design lcd-clock-c1 D7-D8 (as built). `unix` is UTC seconds. The node polls the seconds register (poll_hz, faster near
the expected rollover) and timestamps each rollover in node time: `read` pairs `unix` with `rollover_us`, the node time
at which that second began, and the hub derives the RTC's error against its own clock from that pair (the node does
not know the hub's clock). `set` writes the time so that second `unix` begins at node time `at_us` and clears the
oscillator-stop flag; `valid` is false while that flag is set (the clock lost power), before a first set, and after the
chip's time jumped with no set (a stray write on the bus: `lost_power` fires) until the next set. With
seed_system_time the node's own clock is set from a valid RTC at boot and after each set.

traits.name: resolution_ms
traits.doc: 1000 on the DS3231, which counts whole seconds

config.name: report_s
config.doc: how often unix (and offset_ms) are reported

properties.name: temp_c10
properties.doc: the chip's temperature, refreshed every 64 s

properties.name: offset_ms
properties.doc: reported 0 by the node: the hub computes the offset from read's unix and rollover_us (clock_read)

commands.name: read
commands.doc: The latest reading (never waits for the bus).

result.name: rollover_us
result.doc: node time (esp_timer us) of the last seconds rollover seen

commands.name: set
commands.doc: Second `unix` (2000-2099) begins at node time `at_us` (0 = now): the node waits until then and writes the time in one burst, which restarts the chip's 1 Hz chain, and clears the oscillator-stop flag. INVALID_ARGS for a target more than 2 s ahead or 1 s behind, or a unix outside 2000-2099. It answers at once; the write follows, and `set` fires only when it succeeded (a hub waits for it).

commands.name: set_aging
commands.doc: The aging-offset register: positive slows the clock, about 0.1 ppm per step at 25 degC.

commands.name: inject
commands.doc: Holds `unix` in place of the chip for hold_ms (0 means 1,000; at most 60,000).

events.name: lost_power
events.doc: The oscillator-stop flag was set at boot, or the chip's time jumped with no set: the time is not trustworthy until set.

capabilities.name: fr.node
capabilities.summary: System capability on port 0 of every device (instance "node"): identity, description, reboot, alias, bindings, state resync.

commands.name: describe
commands.doc: Returns the node descriptor (07 §7.4), encoded; HELLO descriptor_hash is FNV-1a 32 over it. BULK: TCP or serial only.

commands.name: set_groups
commands.doc: M2

commands.name: get_state
commands.doc: Re-send every property with fresh LATEST seqs.

commands.name: bind_set
commands.doc: Store a binding in its slot (07 §7.11), replacing what the slot held; the hub resolves and pre-encodes it.

fields.name: on_cls
fields.doc: 3 EVENT | 7 MSG

fields.name: on_kind
fields.doc: the event id (EVENT)

fields.name: on_topic
fields.doc: the MSG topic (MSG)

fields.name: to_addr
fields.doc: this node, another node, or 0xFFFF (MSG broadcast)

fields.name: to_cls
fields.doc: 4 CMD | 7 MSG

fields.name: to_kind
fields.doc: the command id (CMD)

fields.name: to_topic
fields.doc: the MSG topic (MSG)

fields.name: payload
fields.doc: pre-encoded CMD fields, or the MSG data

fields.name: reliable
fields.doc: Q1: ACK_REQ, the target's RESULT or ACK, end-to-end retries

fields.name: slot
fields.doc: 0..15, or 255: every slot

commands.name: bind_list
commands.doc: Returns the stored bindings, encoded (like describe). BULK: TCP or serial only.

events.name: boot
events.doc: Sent once per boot right after the first WELCOME; exempt from the event-age rule.

fields.name: target_status
fields.doc: the target's RESULT/ACK status for reliable sends; 0 for fast, MSG and broadcast; FAILED after the last attempt; BUSY with no path

fields.name: rtt_us
fields.doc: trigger -> target RESULT; 0 for fast commands

fields.name: path
fields.doc: 0 espnow, 1 hub, 2 flood, 3 local (the node itself)

capabilities.name: fr.ota
capabilities.summary: OTA endpoint on port 240 (instance "ota"). Control uses cls=OTA frames (protocol.yaml), not commands.

capabilities.name: fr.diag
capabilities.summary: Diagnostics on port 241 (instance "diag"); the same command set as the serial command channel.

commands.name: exec
commands.doc: Runs one diag command line (info, caps, call, inject, stats, selftest, mark, log, ota, net, pin_pulse, reboot) and returns single-line JSON (BULK).
